This indicates continued community interest and activity surrounding advanced LLMs like Llama 3.1.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
Tags indicate its use of transformers and safetensors formats.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
The associated tags (transformers, llama, safetensors) confirm its relevance within the modern AI/ML ecosystem.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speedup reaches up to 90% when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon utilizing the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also demonstrates reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these personal AI agents entirely on local hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM integration.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance gains.
The integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, optimizing LLM execution on Apple hardware.
This is currently available in a preview state, indicating ongoing development and optimization.

stories.title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B
stories.author: Iliya Mirzaei
bullet_points: Repeated sampling (simple repetition) outperforms complex self-refinement and reflection techniques in LLMs when token costs are equal.
The study suggests that the increased text generation inherent in complex methods might artificially inflate perceived accuracy gains.
The finding challenges the prevailing assumption that complex, multi-step reasoning (like self-critique) is always superior to simpler generation strategies.

stories.title: KAISEN: Reproducible Subgroup Fairness Auditing for Clinical Risk Models
stories.author: Nishita Chavan
bullet_points: Introduces KAISEN, a comprehensive five-phase audit pipeline designed for assessing fairness in clinical risk models.
Addresses the critical issue where high aggregate model performance masks significant, unequal error rates across different patient subgroups.
The pipeline covers stratification, disparity measurement, mechanism diagnostics, mitigation, and drift monitoring to ensure audit reliability.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance enhancements and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine, improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of subagents for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing the model's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing.
The core value proposition is providing private, local AI assistance without reliance on cloud services.

stories.title: Is paying artists enough to convince them to embrace AI?
stories.author: Charles Pulliam-Moore
bullet_points: Generative AI models are being trained on artists' work without explicit permission.
Artists view this practice as theft, while AI proponents argue it is necessary for technological evolution.
The conflict has escalated into contentious legal battles regarding intellectual property rights in AI.

stories.title: As Reddit stock falls, CEO questions value of Google's AI Overviews
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: Reddit is reportedly re-evaluating its licensing agreement with Google.
The uncertainty is linked to recent performance issues and questions surrounding Google's AI Overviews.
The situation highlights growing tension between content providers and major AI developers.

stories.title: Defcon's new badge is a security key you can see inside
stories.author: Kim Zetter, wired.com
bullet_points: Defcon's new badge incorporates a removable chip for enhanced security.
The chip design allows hackers to inspect the badge's internal workings.
A significant security vulnerability exists, enabling badge reuse even after the event.

stories.title: Google plans to exempt sanctioned nations from Android developer verification
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google is planning to exempt sanctioned nations from Android developer verification requirements.
This change means developers in countries like Cuba or Iran can continue installing APKs without new restrictions.
The policy shift is expected to negatively impact developers operating within these sanctioned regions.

stories.title: ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision-Language Models for Visual Retrieval
stories.author: Derek Hoiem
bullet_points: ReToken addresses the computational and performance challenges of long visual context in Vision-Language Models (VLMs).
It introduces a single learnable embedding that acts as an explicit retrieval target to select sparse, query-relevant visual tokens from the KV cache.
The method shows consistent performance gains across image and video benchmarks using only a small dataset.

stories.title: PAC-MAN: Perception-Aware CBF-RL for Whole-Body Safety in Humanoid Dodgeball
stories.author: Aaron D. Ames
bullet_points: Introduces PAC-MAN, a novel Perception-Aware Control Barrier Function Reinforcement Learning (CBF-RL) framework.
Addresses whole-body safety in humanoid robotics by integrating realistic, limited onboard sensing (e.g., segmentation-masked depth) with comprehensive training-time safety constraints.
Applies the framework to a complex physical task, humanoid dodgeball, using adversarial motion priors to enhance evasive reflexes.

stories.title: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis
stories.author: Kyunghyun Cho
bullet_points: AskChem is a new infrastructure designed to improve chemistry literature synthesis by moving beyond simple document retrieval.
It shifts the focus of retrieval from entire papers to specific, provenance-carrying claims within the literature.
The tool aims to automate the manual process scientists currently use to locate, verify, and assemble cross-paper answers.

stories.title: AISPA: User-Centric System Prompt Auditing for Large Language Model Applications
stories.author: Jiaxin Pei
bullet_points: Addresses the critical lack of transparency regarding system prompts, which govern LLM behavior in commercial AI.
Introduces AISPA, a new user-centric framework designed to systematically audit these often-hidden system prompts.
Focuses on closing the trust and accountability gap created by the non-disclosure of these foundational AI instructions.

stories.title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
stories.author: Lingpeng Kong
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical need for standardized evaluation methods for Computer-Using Agents (CUAs).
Current evaluation relies heavily on Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to judge CUA trajectories, but standardization is lacking.
OSReward proposes a framework to institute standardized evaluation for cross-platform CUA reward models.

stories.title: PAIChecker: Uncovering and Checking PR-Issue Misalignment in SWE-Bench-Like Benchmarks
stories.author: Pinjia He
bullet_points: Introduces PAIChecker, a tool designed to identify and check for misalignment between Pull Requests (PRs) and their linked issues.
Addresses a critical flaw in current LLM evaluation benchmarks (like SWE-Bench), where PR-Issue pairings can be incorrectly constructed.
Highlights the practical challenge in maintaining large code repositories, leading to unreliable data for assessing LLM issue resolution capabilities.

stories.title: DualG-MRAG: Decoupling Macro-Reasoning and Micro-Matching for Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
stories.author: Jianxin Li
bullet_points: The paper addresses limitations in Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (MM-RAG), specifically its struggle with complex multi-hop reasoning.
Existing methods often rely on independent instance-level matching, failing to capture cross-modal relationships effectively.
The proposed DualG-MRAG decouples macro-reasoning from micro-matching to overcome the challenges of fine-grained feature integration in graph-enhanced multimodal systems.

stories.title: ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision-Language Models for Visual Retrieval
stories.author: Derek Hoiem
bullet_points: ReToken addresses the computational and performance challenges of long visual context in Vision-Language Models (VLMs).
It introduces a single learnable embedding that acts as an explicit retrieval target to select sparse, query-relevant visual tokens from the KV cache.
The method shows consistent performance gains across image and video benchmarks while requiring training on a small dataset.

stories.title: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis
stories.author: Kyunghyun Cho
bullet_points: AskChem introduces a claim-centered infrastructure to address limitations in traditional chemistry literature search.
It moves beyond simple ranked document lists to allow for the assembly of specific, cross-paper findings.
The system focuses on retrieving provenance-carrying claims rather than entire papers, aiding verification.

stories.title: Change2Task: From Repository Changes to Executable Coding Agent Tasks and Environments
stories.author: Qi Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces Change2Task, a system designed to generate executable coding tasks from repository history.
Addresses the critical need for a continuous supply of realistic, verified data to train and benchmark coding AI agents.
Converts merged pull requests into structured tasks, coupling historical code changes with modern repository states and development tools.

stories.title: MixFrag: Fragility-Guided Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization for Vision Transformers
stories.author: Md. Umar Faruk
bullet_points: Introduces MixFrag, a new mixed-precision Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) framework specifically for Vision Transformers (ViTs).
Addresses the limitation of existing PTQ methods by moving beyond uniform bit-widths, recognizing the heterogeneous sensitivity of different transformer components.
Aims to improve deployment efficiency of ViTs on resource-constrained devices by intelligently allocating precision based on component fragility.

stories.title: $β$-OPSD: Deriving with Policy Optimization, Training with Self-Distillation
stories.author: Furong Huang
bullet_points: The paper addresses the practical brittleness of On-policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) in reasoning language models.
It introduces $\beta$-OPSD, framing OPSD as a specific case ($\beta=1$) within a broader policy-optimization family.
The core contribution is making the KL penalty weighting factor ($\beta$) a controllable parameter to improve reliability.

stories.title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B
stories.author: Iliya Mirzaei
bullet_points: The paper challenges the prevailing trend of complex self-correction methods (like Reflexion) in LLMs.
It suggests that simple, repeated sampling of the same prompt can achieve comparable or better accuracy than elaborate planning/reflection techniques at the same token cost.
This implies that the benefit of generating more text might be an inherent factor in accuracy improvement, rather than the sophistication of the self-refinement mechanism itself.

stories.title: APO: Unsupervised Atomic Policy Optimization for 3D Structure Prediction of Atomic Systems
stories.author: Yatao Bian
bullet_points: The paper introduces APO, an Unsupervised Atomic Policy Optimization method for predicting 3D structures of atomic systems.
It addresses a major bottleneck in material science and drug discovery: the high cost of obtaining labeled data for novel structures.
APO aims to overcome the dependency of existing flow-matching models (like FlowDPO) on supervised preference learning.

stories.title: WCM: A World Critic Model for Vision-Language-Action Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Xipeng Qiu
bullet_points: The paper introduces WCM, a World Critic Model, to address limitations in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) reinforcement learning.
Existing critic-based RL methods struggle with partially observable robot control because they rely on single-frame observations or latent representations.
WCM aims to overcome the exponential complexity issue associated with naively incorporating full observation history into the critic.

stories.title: FriendBench: Benchmarking Dyadic Familiarity Inference in Humans and Multimodal Large Language Models
stories.author: Benjamin Peloquin
bullet_points: Introduces FriendBench, a new benchmark for inferring dyadic familiarity (strangers vs. familiar) from short social interactions.
Evaluates 26 models from seven companies across text, audio, and video modalities against human panels.
Highlights the importance of non-verbal cues and behavior in understanding social dynamics, moving beyond purely textual analysis.

stories.title: ResKV: Reconstructing Omitted Attention Contributions for Fixed-Budget KV Cache Compression
stories.author: Shuo Shang
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical issue of KV cache compression for efficient long-context LLM inference.
Existing compression methods either permanently discard information or perturb retained key/value pairs.
The proposed 'ResKV' method formulates omitted attention contributions as residual statistics to improve compression accuracy.

stories.title: ARB: A Matched Authorship-Rewriting Benchmark Dataset for AI-Text Detector Evaluation
stories.author: Simon Pietro Romano
bullet_points: Introduces ARB, a new benchmark dataset specifically designed for evaluating AI-text detectors.
Addresses a gap in current research by testing how detectors perform when human-written text is rewritten by LLMs, rather than just comparing human vs. raw LLM output.
The dataset is built from 1,800 human source texts, aiming to provide a more realistic evaluation of detector robustness against paraphrasing.

stories.title: Evidence-Type Competition: When Can Interventional Data Teach Language Models Causal Direction?
stories.author: Xining Xun
bullet_points: The paper challenges the assumption that interventional data is always sufficient to teach causal reasoning to language models.
In controlled synthetic environments (Simpson's-paradox worlds), increasing interventional data does not improve the model's ability to infer causal direction.
The study suggests that simply increasing the fraction of interventional samples during pretraining may not guarantee better causal understanding.

stories.title: Know It, Act on It: Investigating Memory Utilization in LLM Personalization
stories.author: Emmanuele Chersoni
bullet_points: Investigates the critical role of memory in making Large Language Models (LLMs) personalized companions.
Addresses the 'knowledge utilization problem' where LLMs may fail to act on relevant user preferences even when the data is in context.
Aims to distinguish between LLMs failing to remember information versus remembering it but failing to apply it correctly.

stories.title: Bridging the Question-Answer Gap in Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Hypothetical Prompt Embeddings
stories.author: Aleksandar Tošić
bullet_points: The paper addresses a core challenge in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): the style mismatch between user queries and retrieved document text.
It proposes a method involving 'Hypothetical Prompt Embeddings' to improve alignment, aiming to overcome limitations of existing runtime solutions like HyDE.
The research focuses on reducing the computational overhead associated with improving query-document relevance in RAG systems.

stories.title: Studying quantization trade-offs for efficient inference deployment in machine translation
stories.author: Teryn Jones
bullet_points: The research addresses the practical challenge of deploying large language models (LLMs) in real-world server environments.
It specifically investigates the trade-offs of quantization—a technique used to reduce model size and improve inference efficiency.
The study evaluates these quantization effects on latency and throughput using two specific machine translation model families.

stories.title: Autoregressive Language Model on the 6502 Processor
stories.author: nmstoker
bullet_points: An autoregressive language model has been successfully implemented on the 6502 processor.
This demonstrates the feasibility of running complex AI models on extremely low-power, legacy hardware.
The project is highly relevant to embedded AI and resource-constrained computing.

stories.title: Show HN: Kakehashi – Experimental userspace to run macOS binaries on Linux ARM
stories.author: vlad_kalinkin
bullet_points: Kakehashi is an experimental userspace project.
Its goal is to run macOS binaries on Linux ARM architecture.
This represents a niche but technically interesting cross-platform compatibility effort.

stories.title: Your AI Agent's Chat History Is User Input
stories.author: y11t0
bullet_points: A functional jailbreak technique has been discovered affecting numerous production chat assistants.
The vulnerability reportedly does not require complex or 'clever' prompts to exploit.
The core issue relates to how AI agents handle and process their own chat history as user input.

stories.title: What I Learned Shipping 90+ Mobile Apps with AI Coding Agents
stories.author: mashi_mashi_3092153ef1ab5
bullet_points: The author has shipped over 90 mobile applications in the past year.
The development process heavily involved the use of AI coding agents.
The article details lessons learned from scaling mobile app development with AI assistance.
